arxiv-1908-11420.title: Exponentiating virtual imaginary contributions in a parton shower Preprint: DESY 19-143
arxiv-1908-11420.creator: Zoltán Nagy, Davison E. Soper
arxiv-1908-11420.description: Abstract The operator in a parton shower algorithm that represents the imaginary part of virtual Feynman graphs has a non-trivial color structure and is large because it is proportional to a factor of 4 ​ π 4\pi . In order to improve the treatment of color in a parton shower, it may help to exponentiate this phase operator.

arxiv-2007-00335.title: Predicting Oxidation and Spin States by High-Dimensional Neural Networks: Applications to Lithium Manganese Oxide Spinels
arxiv-2007-00335.creator: Marco Eckhoff, Knut Nikolas Lausch, Peter E. Blöchl, Jörg Behler
arxiv-2007-00335.description: Abstract Lithium ion batteries often contain transition metal oxides like Li x Mn 2 O 4 ( 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 0\leq x\leq 2 ). Depending on the Li content different ratios of Mn III {}^{\text{III}} to Mn IV {}^{\text{IV}} ions are present.

arxiv-2108-06032.title: Unconventional rheological properties in systems of deformable particles
arxiv-2108-06032.creator: Anshuman Pasupalak, Shawn Khuhan Samidurai, Yanwei Li, Yuanjian Zheng, Ran Ni, Massimo Pica Ciamarra
arxiv-2108-06032.description: Abstract We demonstrate the existence of unconventional rheological and memory properties in systems of soft-deformable particles whose energy depends on their shape, via numerical simulations. At large strains, these systems experience an unconventional shear weakening transition characterized by an increase in the mechanical energy and a drastic drop in shear stress, which stems from the emergence of short-ranged tetratic order.

arxiv-2210-15876.title: Random Utterance Concatenation Based Data Augmentation for Improving Short-video Speech Recognition
arxiv-2210-15876.creator: Yist Y. Lin ∗ , Tao Han ∗ , Haihua Xu ∗ , Van Tung Pham, Yerbolat Khassanov, Tze Yuang Chong, Yi He, Lu Lu, Zejun Ma
arxiv-2210-15876.description: Abstract One of limitations in end-to-end automatic speech recognition (ASR) framework is its performance would be compromised if train-test utterance lengths are mismatched. In this paper, we propose an on-the-fly random utterance concatenation (RUC) based data augmentation method to alleviate train-test utterance length mismatch issue for short-video ASR task.

arxiv-2305-14502.title: RetICL: Sequential Retrieval of In-Context Examples with Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2305-14502.creator: Alexander Scarlatos, Andrew Lan
arxiv-2305-14502.description: Abstract Recent developments in large pre-trained language models have enabled unprecedented performance on a variety of downstream tasks. Achieving best performance with these models often leverages in-context learning, where a model performs a (possibly new) task given one or more examples.

arxiv-2312-15181.title: Multilingual Bias Detection and Mitigation for Indian Languages
arxiv-2312-15181.creator: Ankita Maity, Anubhav Sharma, Rudra Dhar, Tushar Abhishek, Manish Gupta, Vasudeva Varma
arxiv-2312-15181.description: Abstract Lack of diverse perspectives causes neutrality bias in Wikipedia content leading to millions of worldwide readers getting exposed by potentially inaccurate information. Hence, neutrality bias detection and mitigation is a critical problem. Although previous studies have proposed effective solutions for English, no work exists for Indian languages.

arxiv-2405-04346.title: Revisiting Character-level Adversarial Attacks for Language Models
arxiv-2405-04346.creator: Elias Abad Rocamora, Yongtao Wu, Fanghui Liu, Grigorios G. Chrysos, Volkan Cevher
arxiv-2405-04346.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Elias Abad Rocamora, Yongtao Wu, Fanghui Liu, Grigorios G. Chrysos, Volkan Cevher. Adversarial attacks in Natural Language Processing apply perturbations in the character or token levels. Token-level attacks, gaining prominence for their use of gradient-based methods, are susceptible to altering sentence semantics, leading to invalid adversarial examples. While character-level attacks easily maintain semantics, they have received less attention as they cannot easily adopt popular gradient-based methods, and are thought to be easy to defend.

arxiv-2406-18528.title: PrExMe! Large Scale Prompt Exploration of Open Source LLMs for Machine Translation and Summarization Evaluation
arxiv-2406-18528.creator: Christoph Leiter, Steffen Eger Natural Language Learning Group (NLLG) https://nl2g.github.io/
arxiv-2406-18528.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Christoph Leiter, Steffen Eger Natural Language Learning Group (NLLG) https://nl2g.github.io/. Large language models ( LLMs ) have revolutionized NLP research . Notably, in-context learning enables their use as evaluation metrics for natural language generation, making them particularly advantageous in low-resource scenarios and time-restricted applications.

arxiv-2408-00004.title: Handling Numeric Expressions in Automatic Speech Recognition
arxiv-2408-00004.creator: Christian Huber, Alexander Waibel
arxiv-2408-00004.description: Abstract This paper addresses the problem of correctly formatting numeric expressions in automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts. This is challenging since the expected transcript format depends on the context, e.g., 1945 (year) vs. 19:45 (timestamp). We compare cascaded and end-to-end approaches to recognize and format numeric expression, such as years, timestamps, currency amounts, and quantities.

arxiv-2504-10879.title: Strain effect on optical properties and quantum weight of 2D magnetic topological insulators MnBi 2 X 4 (X = Te, Se, S)
arxiv-2504-10879.creator: Nguyen Tuan Hung, Vuong Van Thanh, Mingda Li, Takahiro Shimada
arxiv-2504-10879.description: Abstract Manipulating the optical and quantum properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials through strain engineering is not only fundamentally interesting but also provides significant benefits across various applications. In this work, we employ first-principles calculations to investigate the effects of strain on the magnetic and optical properties of 2D topological insulators MnBi 2 X 4 (X = Te, Se, S).

arxiv-2506-09178.title: Understanding Self-Regulated Learning Behavior Among High and Low Dropout Risk Students During CS1: Combining Trace Logs, Dropout Prediction and Self-Reports CCS: Social and professional topics CS1
arxiv-2506-09178.creator: Denis Zhidkikh, Ville Isomöttönen, Toni Taipalus
arxiv-2506-09178.description: Abstract . The introductory programming course (CS1) at the university level is often perceived as particularly challenging, contributing to high dropout rates among Computer Science students. Identifying when and how students encounter difficulties in this course is critical for providing targeted support.

arxiv-2510-09759.description: Abstract Polarized synchrotron emission at meter to centimeter wavelengths provides an effective tracer of the Galactic magnetic field. Calculating Faraday depth, the most useful parameter for mapping the line-of-sight magnetic field, requires observations covering wide frequency bands with many channels.

arxiv-2510-23812.title: The Goresky-Hingston Coproduct on Based Loop Spaces
arxiv-2510-23812.creator: Jonathan Clivio
arxiv-2510-23812.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jonathan Clivio. We construct a lift of the Goresky-Hingston coproduct on the based loop space. Using this lift, we produce formulas for the interaction of the coproduct with the π 1 \pi_{1} -action and with maps of manifolds. These results lets us compute the coproduct on the based loop space for manifolds of the form S n / G S^{n}/G .

pmc-10609139.title: Photoluminescence of Cesium-Doped Sodium Iodide Films Irradiated by UV LED
pmc-10609139.creator: Hsing-Yu Wu, Yu-Hung Kuan, Guoyu Yu, Yung-Shin Sun, Jin-Cherng Hsu, Junying Zhang
pmc-10609139.description: Alkali metal halides have long been used as scintillators for applications as sensors and detectors. Usually, a small amount of impurities are added to these inorganic materials to improve their luminescence efficiencies. We investigate the structures and luminescent properties of un-doped sodium iodide (NaI) and cesium-doped NaI (NaI:Cs) films deposited by thermal vacuum evaporation.

pmc-11479979.title: Temporal and spatial analysis of event-related potentials in response to color saliency differences among various color vision types
pmc-11479979.creator: Naoko Takahashi, Masataka Sawayama, Xu Chen, Yuki Motomura, Hiroshige Takeichi, Satoru Miyauchi, Chihiro Hiramatsu
pmc-11479979.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionHuman color vision exhibits significant diversity that cannot be fully explained by categorical classifications. Understanding how individuals with different color vision phenotypes perceive, recognize, and react to the same physical stimuli provides valuable insights into sensory characteristics.

pmc-11491708.title: Protocol to characterize mouse dural mast cells by flow cytometry and immunofluorescence
pmc-11491708.creator: Chih-Chung Jerry Lin, Nader Jaafar, Rudolph E. Tanzi
pmc-11491708.description: SummaryMast cells, which constitute tissue-resident immune cells, are distributed in the dural meninges. Here, we provide procedural guidelines for investigating mouse dural mast cells using two techniques. First, we outline the procedures for dural tissue dissection, single-cell isolation, and subsequent surface staining for mast cell identification via flow cytometry.

pmc-11715059.title: From glia to cytokine signatures across the Alzheimer’s spectrum
pmc-11715059.creator: Maura Malpetti, Peter Swann, Leonidas Chouliaras, P Simon Jones, Elijah Mak, W Richard Bevan‐Jones, Li Su, Tim D Fryer, Young T Hong, Franklin I Aigbirhio, John T O'Brien, James B Rowe
pmc-11715059.description: BackgroundEarly neuroinflammation is involved in pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) and contributes to faster clinical decline. Thus, neuroinflammation has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for dementia. However, a better understanding of the interaction between central and peripheral inflammation in human disease and in vivo biomarkers are required for successful clinical trials.

pmc-11976083.title: Patterns of mandibular third molar impaction and its relationship with distal caries in the adjacent mandibular second molars: A retrospective study
pmc-11976083.creator: Abrar K Demyati
pmc-11976083.description: BackgroundImpacted third molars can cause significant challenges for dental health. While many of these impacted teeth remain asymptomatic, they can lead to dental caries.ObjectiveTo investigate the patterns of mandibular third molar impaction and its relationship with the occurrence of caries in the adjacent mandibular second molars.

pmc-13062007.title: Unmasking non-malarial mosquito-borne infections among febrile children in malaria-endemic regions of western Kenya
pmc-13062007.creator: Jack Ogony, Simon Karanja, George Ayodo, Ivy Akinyi, Daniel Onguru, Charles Angira, Diana Menya, Judith Mangeni
pmc-13062007.description: Almost half of under-five children in health facilities are febrile in sub-Saharan Africa. The non-specific clinical symptoms coupled with; limited diagnostics capacities, overlapping endemicity and the surveillance gaps complicates accurate cause identification of an acute febrile illnesses in resource limited settings. This challenge leads to misdiagnosis, overtreatment, and delays in appropriate management, increasing morbidity and mortality.

pmc-13271096.title: Standardizing attenuation across tube voltages and vertebral levels for opportunistic osteoporosis screening on low-dose chest CT
pmc-13271096.creator: Youngjune Kim, Sehyun Hong, Choong Guen Chee, Yusuhn Kang, Eugene Lee, Yeo Ju Kim, Joon Woo Lee
pmc-13271096.description: BackgroundOpportunistic screening of osteoporosis on CT has emerged as a cost-effective strategy for bone health assessment. However, vertebral attenuation varies substantially with CT tube voltage and spinal level, limiting standardization.PurposeTo model and standardize vertebral attenuation across tube voltages and spinal levels on low-dose chest CT for opportunistic osteoporosis screening.

pmc-13350663.title: Persistent Hypoxia After Tricuspid Valve Replacement
pmc-13350663.creator: John Nguyen, Thomas Merino, Vijay Kandula, Leticia Castillo Kontak, Raul Mercado Garcia, Angel Caldera, Aditi Shankar, Rafael Gonzalez, Soumya Neravetla, Jose F Condado
pmc-13350663.description: BackgroundTranscatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) is a novel therapy for symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation in high-risk surgical patients. Platypnea-orthopnea syndrome has not previously been described as a complication of TTVR.Case SummaryA 76-year-old woman with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation underwent successful TTVR but developed persistent hypoxia despite negative pulmonary work-up. Her hypoxia followed a platypnea-orthodeoxia pattern.
